Ask someone their sign and they'll give you the Sun. Ask their closest friend what they're like at 2 am after bad news, and you'll get the Moon.

The Moon sign is the part of the chart that runs when nobody's watching: what you need to feel safe, how you react before you've had time to think, what "home" means to you. It's also the fastest-moving thing in the chart, which makes it the one most likely to be wrong if the birth time is off. This guide covers what it means, how to check it, and how to read it alongside the Sun.

doan: The Moon sign is the zodiac sign the Moon was in at the moment you were born. The Moon takes about 27.3 days to go around the whole zodiac, so it spends roughly two and a half days in each sign.

Where the Sun describes what you're consciously becoming, the Moon describes what you already are when you stop trying. Habits, reflexes, comfort. It's the sign that shows up in how you handle hunger, tiredness, and stress, which is most of daily life.
Planet Moon Rules Cancer Emotions, intuition, nurturing
House House 4 Family, ancestry, emotional foundation, private life, endings

muc.ten: Why it can change within a single day
doan: The Moon moves about 12 to 15 degrees a day. Since each sign is 30 degrees wide, the Moon changes sign roughly every 2.5 days, and on the day it changes, the hour matters.

If you were born on a "Moon change" day, someone born at 7 am and someone born at 10 pm can have different Moon signs. The two descriptions will read very differently. Cancer Moon at 7 am: needs closeness, remembers everything. Leo Moon at 10 pm: needs to be seen, forgets grudges faster.

Quick check: run your chart with 00:01 and 23:59 on your birth date. If the Moon sign is the same both times, you're safe regardless of birth time. If it differs, you'll need to narrow the time, or read both descriptions and be honest about which one is you.
Emotional reflexes. Your first reaction, before the Sun gets a vote.
Needs. What has to be true for you to relax. Taurus Moon needs things to be stable. Gemini Moon needs something interesting to happen.
Comfort and habits. Food, sleep, routines, the things you reach for when tired.
Memory and the past. The Moon holds the childhood layer of the chart, and the model of "mother" or the primary caretaker.
Home. Not the address, the feeling. What makes a place yours.
The body's rhythms. Traditional astrology links the Moon to digestion, fluids, and the cyclical parts of health.
Each line: what it needs, and what it does under stress.
Aries Moon: needs action and independence. Under stress, gets angry fast and forgets fast.
Taurus Moon: needs stability and physical comfort. Under stress, digs in and won't move.
Gemini Moon: needs to talk it out and stay stimulated. Under stress, gets scattered and over-explains.
Cancer Moon: needs closeness and to feel needed. Under stress, withdraws into the shell.
Leo Moon: needs warmth and recognition. Under stress, gets dramatic or goes quiet in a way you're meant to notice.
Virgo Moon: needs order and usefulness. Under stress, worries, criticizes, cleans.
Libra Moon: needs harmony and company. Under stress, avoids conflict until it can't.
Scorpio Moon: needs depth and loyalty. Under stress, goes silent and watches.
Sagittarius Moon: needs freedom and meaning. Under stress, leaves, literally or mentally.
Capricorn Moon: needs to be competent and in control. Under stress, works harder and says it's fine.
Aquarius Moon: needs space and intellectual distance. Under stress, detaches and analyzes.
Pisces Moon: needs escape and gentleness. Under stress, absorbs everything and gets overwhelmed.
This is where the Moon sign gets useful. Compare it to the Sun.
Same element (both fire, both earth, etc.): the conscious self and the emotional self want similar things. Life feels internally consistent, sometimes to the point of blind spots.
Compatible elements (fire with air, earth with water): the two parts of you cooperate. The Sun leads, the Moon supports.

Clashing elements (fire with water, earth with air, and so on): you want one thing and need another. A Sagittarius Sun with a Cancer Moon wants adventure and needs home. This isn't a flaw; it's why some people have such a rich inner life. But it helps to name it.

Also check the aspect between them. Sun square Moon: the tension is active and shows up as restlessness. Sun trine Moon: it's smoothed over, sometimes too smoothly. Sun conjunct Moon: born near a New Moon, the two are fused, strong sense of self, less internal debate.
There's a full cheat sheet for Sun-Moon pairs in the compatibility guide on this site, written for two-chart reads, but it works just as well for reading the pair inside one chart.
If you have a reliable birth time, the Moon's house says where you go for comfort.
1st: you wear your feelings; people can read you.
4th: home and family are the whole emotional world.
7th: partnership is where you feel safe, for better or worse.
10th: work and reputation carry emotional weight; being useful in public matters.
12th: the emotional life is private, sometimes even from yourself.
The others follow the house meanings. The Moon in the 6th finds comfort in routine and being of use. In the 9th, in travel, learning, and big ideas.
One more layer that most sign descriptions skip: where the Moon was in its cycle when you were born.
Born near a New Moon (Sun and Moon in the same sign or close): self-contained, starts things, less need for outside approval.
Born near a Full Moon (Sun and Moon opposite): pulled between two poles, very aware of other people, tends to find themselves through relationships.
Born on a waxing Moon (between New and Full): building, forward-looking. On a waning Moon (Full back to New): reflective, more interested in meaning than momentum.
You can check this with the moon phase tool by entering your birth date.
Open the birth chart tool → and look at the Moon glyph. The tool shows sign, house, and every aspect the Moon makes, with orbs.

If your birth time is uncertain, do the 00:01 and 23:59 test first. If the Moon sign holds, read it with confidence. If it doesn't, read both. For most people, one of the two descriptions lands immediately, because the Moon is the part of you that other people have been describing to you your whole life.
